Salam,


  • Context: Quality HVAC runs seasonal tune-up campaigns targeting existing customers twice a year (spring for AC, fall for heating). This is the text sequence to support that offer. Aiman confirmed copy and timing during the 8/27 meeting.

  • Deliverable: Build a GHL text campaign with the following messages, spaced 3 days apart:

    • Message 1: "Hi [First Name], it's time for your seasonal tune-up! Quality HVAC is offering $89 tune-ups this month (regularly $149). Keep your system running smoothly before the season hits. Reply YES to schedule or give us a call."

    • Message 2 (if no reply): "Just a reminder—our $89 tune-up special ends soon. A quick check now can save you from expensive repairs later. Reply YES or call us to book your appointment."

    • Message 3 (if no reply): "Last chance for $89 tune-ups! This offer expires very soon! Quality HVAC—[business phone]. Reply STOP to opt out."



  • Trigger: Contact receives tag "Tune Up Campaign" in GHL. No other prerequisites—existing customers are already in the system.

  • Success criteria: Campaign live in GHL, all three messages scheduled correctly with 3-day intervals, tested on a dummy contact, and Aiman confirms he can see it firing as expected.

body:
Salam,

  • Context: the 27 August five month review put hard numbers on the intake problem. 65 percent of inbound calls are missed and 78 percent of those arrive outside office hours. Only 20 percent of inbound texts and Instagram messages get a human reply. Against $8,200 of ad spend and 84 leads in the period, that intake gap is what is driving cost per lead up, not the campaigns. Callbacks are currently made outside GHL, so there is no record of who was chased or how many times.

  •  Log every call attempt as a note on the opportunity so attempt counts are queryable. Add a Junk stage so spam and marketing calls are filtered out instead of inflating lead counts.

  • Automation: send a second missed call text five minutes after the first to widen the engagement window on the after hours volume. Build a notification workflow that alerts the team member (assigned or Luis) when a lead responds, so replies are picked up in real time rather than at the next inbox check. Push the centralised lead inbox and the GHL mobile app so those alerts actually land.

  • Done = the GHL pipeline carries Attempted Contact, Engaged and Junk stages, every call attempt writes a note on the opportunity, a second missed call text fires five minutes after the first, team members are notified on lead responses, Luis is working callbacks inside GHL, and the missed call backlog is cleared.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

The 24 August go live checkin asked for a manual push button inside GHL that sends a selected contact into Clio Manage, creating both the Clio contact and the matter in one action, with an update due before the Maadi Law onboarding call. Today everything moves by hand, which is the main friction Tracy's intake flow still has.
  • Build the button. It triggers on a selected GHL contact, checks first for an existing Clio Contact ID on that record, then creates the Clio contact and the associated matter, writes the returned Clio Contact ID and Matter ID back onto the GHL contact, and logs any failure visibly rather than failing silently. A second press on the same contact must update the existing Clio records rather than create a second matter.
  • Constraints. Do not touch the historical owner mapping table that was already imported and keep the first phase one way from GHL into Clio for this button so it does not collide with the Clio to GHL owner sync being built on the sibling subitem. Clio API credentials are needed before step two can start.
  • done = pressing the button on a GHL contact creates exactly one matching Clio Manage contact and one matter, both ids written back onto the GHL contact, and a second press on the same contact updates rather than duplicating, verified on a test case.

body:
Salam,

  • Context. During the 8/28 go live session Tracy created contacts and opportunities live from the GHL intake form and hit several field problems that stop her entering real leads. Email is a required field today, but a large share of the phone leads never give one. There is no way to record what kind of record a contact is, which matters for a personal injury practice where treaters and insurers sit in the same database as leads. The form also still carries a ready to sign checkbox left over from the testing phase.
  • Make phone the only required field and email optional, so a caller with no email address can still be saved as a contact and an opportunity.
  • Add a contact type dropdown with lead, customer, treater, insurance and health insurance as the options.
  • Remove the ready to sign checkbox and any other leftover test fields from the form.
  • Added language tags using the shorthand agreed in the session, AR for Arabic and SP for Spanish, so bilingual leads can be routed to a case manager who speaks the language. Allow tagging from form.
  • Dependencies and constraints. The contact type values and the language tag strings are read by the case manager routing and welcome message automations, so lock the exact strings before building either side. No dependency on the Clio Manage sync work, this can start immediately.
  • Done. Tracy can create a contact from the intake form with no email address, pick a contact type from the dropdown, and apply an AR or SP language tag, with no test fields left on the form.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

A representation agreement generated from a GHL contact opens with location of incident already filled from the contact record or filled by Tracy in the intake form, I a signature date that populates itself at signing, and Sharif's signature box already placed and assigned, with zero manual edits between generating the document and sending it.

body:
Salam,

  • Context. At the 24 August go live checkin the NextGen to GHL appointment sync was confirmed running on the separate DigitalOcean instance that keeps MedStation patient data isolated for HIPAA, pushing appointment status into GHL every 15 minutes. Final verification against live data is still outstanding, and this is one of the last pieces of the Weston pilot that has not been signed off.
  • Defect one, duplicate appointments. Rescheduling in NextGen produces two appointment records in GHL instead of one. The working theory from the session is that the sync account has read and write rights on the mirror but no delete right, so the superseded appointment is never removed. The team has not yet ruled out genuine double bookings by patients, so this needs confirming with MedStation before any logic changes.
  • Defect two, source overwrite. The sync currently writes the contact source field on contacts it touches, which wipes the original Google Ads, Meta Ads or LSA attribution the moment a patient books. Every synced contact ends up looking like it came from NextGen.
  • Verify the appointment status sync end to end against live NextGen data and confirm each status change lands in GHL inside the 15 minute window.
  • Request and confirm delete permission for the sync account on the NextGen mirror, then reproduce a reschedule and a cancellation and confirm GHL holds exactly one current appointment record afterwards.
  • Modify the sync so it no longer writes contact source on an existing contact, and add the tag "Next Gen Sync" to every contact it touches so NextGen originated records stay identifiable without destroying campaign attribution.
  • Dependencies. Depends on the DigitalOcean mirror connection staying stable and on MedStation IT granting delete rights, which sits outside our control.
  • done = a rescheduled or cancelled NextGen appointment leaves exactly one matching appointment record in GHL with no duplicate, and a contact that syncs from NextGen keeps its original source value and carries the "Next Gen Sync" tag.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer
